root_cause.text: In intel_pstate, the max-frequency update path iterated over possible CPUs and passed all_cpu_data[cpu] directly, so offline/limited CPUs with NULL all_cpu_data entries were dereferenced after the 973207ae3d7c refactor.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that for_each_possible_cpu() includes CPUs that are not online, “for those CPUs, all_cpu_data[] will be NULL,” and the patch changes intel_pstate_update_max_freq() from taking struct cpudata * to taking an int cpu, first calling cpufreq_cpu_get(cpu) and only then using all_cpu_data[cpu] when there is a valid policy.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor max-frequency update helper to take a CPU ID and look up the canonical per-CPU data internally instead of relying on a passed cpudata pointer.
intent_record.what: The helper function signature was changed from taking a `struct cpudata *cpudata` parameter to taking an `int cpu` parameter. Inside the function, `cpufreq_cpu_get()` now uses `cpu` instead of `cpudata->cpu`, and the call to `__intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` now passes `all_cpu_data[cpu]` instead of the original `cpudata` argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now derives the per-CPU data structure from the global `all_cpu_data` array using the CPU number after successfully obtaining the policy for that CPU. This avoids depending on a caller-provided `cpudata` pointer and ensures the update uses the canonical per-CPU state associated with the requested CPU.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix intel_pstate_update_limits_for_all() to pass the CPU ID, not per-CPU data, when updating max frequency for all CPUs.
intent_record.what: The loop in intel_pstate_update_limits_for_all() was changed so that intel_pstate_update_max_freq() is called with the CPU index variable cpu instead of all_cpu_data[cpu].
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now passes the expected CPU identifier to intel_pstate_update_max_freq() for each possible CPU, ensuring the per-CPU max frequency update uses the correct argument rather than a per-CPU data pointer or entry, which would lead to incorrect behavior or a type mismatch in execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix intel_pstate_notify_work() to call intel_pstate_update_max_freq() with the CPU id instead of a cpudata pointer.
intent_record.what: The call to intel_pstate_update_max_freq() inside intel_pstate_notify_work() was changed to pass cpudata->cpu instead of the cpudata pointer itself.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now receives the CPU identifier it expects rather than a cpudata structure pointer, allowing the max-frequency update logic to operate on the correct CPU and avoiding incorrect behavior from passing an argument of the wrong type or meaning.

Fix intel_pstate_notify_work() to call intel_pstate_update_max_freq() with the CPU id instead of a cpudata pointer.

consistency_review.core_intent: Correct intel_pstate call sites to pass a CPU ID rather than a per-CPU cpudata pointer when updating maximum frequency limits.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by avoiding use of potentially NULL all_cpu_data[cpu] pointers in the max-frequency update path and instead looking up the canonical per-CPU data from the CPU ID inside the helper.

The root cause is that max-frequency update paths passed all_cpu_data[cpu] directly, leading to NULL dereferences for offline/limited CPUs. These changes specifically fix the affected call sites to pass the CPU ID instead of the per-CPU cpudata pointer when updating max frequency, directly addressing that cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct vulnerable call site: it iterates over all possible CPUs and passes all_cpu_data[cpu] without checking for NULL, so offline/limited CPUs with NULL entries can be dereferenced in the callee.
This dereferences cpudata immediately via cpudata->cpu. When the caller passes a NULL all_cpu_data[cpu] entry, this statement triggers the NULL-pointer dereference.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call iterates over possible CPUs and passes all_cpu_data[cpu] directly into the max-frequency update helper without validating that the per-CPU pointer is non-NULL. After the refactor, offline or otherwise unavailable CPUs could have NULL all_cpu_data entries, making this the vulnerable statement that feeds a NULL pointer into the callee.

This statement dereferences cpudata via cpudata->cpu immediately on entry to the helper. When the caller supplies a NULL all_cpu_data[cpu] pointer, this line triggers the NULL-pointer dereference described in the root cause.

The vulnerable construct is present in `intel_pstate_update_limits_for_all()`: `for_each_possible_cpu(cpu) intel_pstate_update_max_freq(all_cpu_data[cpu]);`. Per the root cause, iterating over possible CPUs and passing `all_cpu_data[cpu]` directly is unsafe because some possible/offline CPUs may have `all_cpu_data[cpu] == NULL`. The new `intel_pstate_update_max_freq(struct cpudata *cpudata)` immediately dereferences `cpudata` with `policy = cpufreq_cpu_get(cpudata->cpu);` before any NULL check on `cpudata`, so a NULL entry would be dereferenced. The function only checks `if (!policy) return false;`, which does not protect against `cpudata == NULL` because the dereference happens earlier. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present. The fix is not present because there is no validation of `cpudata` before dereferencing it, nor is there filtering of CPUs to avoid NULL `all_cpu_data` entries in the all-CPU iteration path.

The vulnerable construct is present in the new helper path: `static void intel_pstate_update_limits_for_all(void) { int cpu; for_each_possible_cpu(cpu) intel_pstate_update_limits(cpu); }` and then `static void intel_pstate_update_limits(unsigned int cpu) { struct cpufreq_policy *policy = cpufreq_cpu_acquire(cpu); if (!policy) return; __intel_pstate_update_max_freq(all_cpu_data[cpu], policy); cpufreq_cpu_release(policy); }`. The root cause says the bug occurs when iterating over possible CPUs and passing `all_cpu_data[cpu]` directly, because some possible/offline/limited CPUs may have `NULL` entries. That exact pattern is here: `for_each_possible_cpu(cpu)` combined with `__intel_pstate_update_max_freq(all_cpu_data[cpu], policy);` with no NULL check on `all_cpu_data[cpu]`. The function `__intel_pstate_update_max_freq()` immediately dereferences `cpudata` via `intel_pstate_get_hwp_cap(cpudata);` and then accesses `cpudata->pstate.max_freq` / `cpudata->pstate.turbo_freq`, so passing a NULL `all_cpu_data[cpu]` would be unsafe. There is no fix in this snippet to validate `all_cpu_data[cpu]` before use or to iterate only over CPUs guaranteed to have valid `cpudata`, so the fix is not present.
